subject.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups

question: Should subscription-auth helper dispatch remain an optional RunEmbeddedAgentParams mode with Claude-specific core policy, or should the eligibility capability live on the registered CLI backend and become the canonical helper-routing seam?
rationale: Both shapes can fix this bug, but the choice defines a trusted plugin runtime API, provider ownership, auth-selection policy, and the relationship to the broader CLI-helper routing work; code inspection cannot determine the intended permanent boundary.

options.title: Backend-owned capability
options.body: Move subscription-dispatch eligibility onto the registered CLI backend and make embedded helpers consume that generic capability, avoiding Claude-specific policy in core.

options.title: Approve narrow core mode
options.body: Keep the optional core dispatch parameter scoped to Claude CLI, with explicit owner approval and focused compatibility and security tests for the public runtime contract.

options.title: Unify with canonical routing issue
options.body: Pause this PR and implement active-memory together with the remaining helper paths tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57326 through one shared dispatch decision.

recommendation.title: Backend-owned capability
recommendation.body: Move subscription-dispatch eligibility onto the registered CLI backend and make embedded helpers consume that generic capability, avoiding Claude-specific policy in core.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses core agent routing, provider ownership, plugin runtime API, and security boundaries rather than belonging only to the Active Memory plugin.
